Passage: The Marrow Point lighthouse was built in 1889 after three coastal ships were lost on the same reef in a single winter. Its lamp originally burned whale oil, but the keepers switched to kerosene in 1911, which made the light brighter and cut the need for deliveries by half. In 1962 the station was automated, and the last keeper, Helen Voss, left the island in the spring of that year. The tower is still standing, though the lamp now runs on electricity and is checked by radio from the mainland.

Passage: The Eastfield Library lends books for three weeks. Members may renew an item once, but only if no one has reserved it. Late returns cost ten cents per day per book, and fines above five dollars block further borrowing until they are paid. Rare manuscripts never leave the reading room. Children under twelve may borrow up to four books at a time, while adults may borrow up to twelve.

Passage: Inspectors examined the Calder Bridge in March. They found cracks in two of the six support piers, both near the waterline, and measured the cracks at 2 and 4 millimeters wide. The engineers decided that cracks under 3 millimeters could be monitored, while wider cracks required the pier to be repaired before the bridge could carry heavy trucks. The repair of the wider crack began in June and finished in August.
